content.text: Detective Raymond investigates Hannah’s sudden death at Mrs. Belden’s house. Q discovers letters, while Raymond finds Hannah’s apparent confession beneath her body, implicating a handsome black-mustached man. Gryce proves the confession forged: it was written on paper taken from Mary Leavenworth’s home and concealed in a letter sent to Hannah. Evidence initially points to Mary, but Gryce stages an interview in a gloomy upstairs room, secretly summoning Henry Clavering and Trueman Harwell. Harwell bursts from a concealed room, admits murdering Horatio Leavenworth and forcing Hannah’s suicide, then confesses fully. He killed Leavenworth in the library, manipulated Hannah into drinking poison in her room, and forged the confession. Mary is exonerated, reconciles with Eleanore, and relinquishes the tainted fortune to charity. The appended essays advocate reason, science, liberty, secular government, abolition, honest money, education, and humanitarian progress while attacking religious dogma, slavery, and eternal punishment.
